objects.definition:
typedef unsigned char Byte;
typedef Byte Bytef;
objects.description: Unsigned 8-bit byte type used by zlib-ng APIs. Bytef is an alias kept for compatibility indicating a pointer to byte data in some APIs.

objects.definition:
typedef unsigned int   uInt;  /* 16 bits or more */
typedef uInt  uIntf;
objects.description: Unsigned integer type used in the API where at least 16 bits are required. uIntf is a compatibility alias.

objects.definition:
typedef unsigned long  uLong; /* 32 bits or more */
typedef uLong uLongf;
objects.description: Unsigned long integer type used by legacy-style APIs. uLongf is a compatibility alias.
Compatibility typedef for char used in some historical zlib APIs.
Compatibility typedef for int used in some historical zlib APIs.
Pointer-to-const-void compatibility typedef used in some APIs. Note: ptr_type here is 'voidpc *' (pointer to the alias type); the alias itself is a const void pointer.
Pointer-to-void compatibility typedef used by some allocation APIs. ptr_type shown is a pointer to the alias type.
Compatibility typedef for void* used across the API. ptr_type shown is pointer to the alias type.
Offset type used by zlib-ng for file positions and lengths. Defined as long unless overridden by platform headers earlier.

objects.definition:
#if !defined(_WIN32) && defined(Z_LARGE64)
#  define z_off64_t off64_t
#else
#  if defined(__MSYS__)
#    define z_off64_t _off64_t
#  elif defined(_WIN32) && !defined(__GNUC__)
#    define z_off64_t __int64
#  else
#    define z_off64_t z_off_t
#  endif
#endif
objects.description: 64-bit offset type used by zlib-ng when large-file support is enabled. Maps to platform-specific 64-bit offset or falls back to z_off_t.

objects.definition: typedef void *(*alloc_func) (void *opaque, unsigned int items, unsigned int size);
objects.description: Function pointer type for custom allocator callbacks used by zlib-ng. Returns a memory block for items * size bytes.
Function pointer type for custom free callbacks used by zlib-ng.

objects.definition:
struct internal_state;

typedef struct zng_stream_s {
    const uint8_t         *next_in;   /* next input byte */
    uint32_t              avail_in;   /* number of bytes available at next_in */
    size_t                total_in;   /* total number of input bytes read so far */

    uint8_t               *next_out;  /* next output byte will go here */
    uint32_t              avail_out;  /* remaining free space at next_out */
    size_t                total_out;  /* total number of bytes output so far */

    const char            *msg;       /* last error message, NULL if no error */
    struct internal_state *state;     /* not visible by applications */

    alloc_func            zalloc;     /* used to allocate the internal state */
    free_func             zfree;      /* used to free the internal state */
    void                  *opaque;    /* private data object passed to zalloc and zfree */

    int                   data_type;  /* best guess about the data type: binary or text
                                         for deflate, or the decoding state for inflate */
    uint32_t              adler;      /* Adler-32 or CRC-32 value of the uncompressed data */
    unsigned long         reserved;   /* reserved for future use */
} zng_stream;

typedef zng_stream *zng_streamp;  /* Obsolete type, retained for compatibility only */
objects.description: Primary stream state structure for zlib-ng compression/decompression. Holds input/output buffers, allocation callbacks, checksum, state, and progress counters. Applications must initialize zalloc/zfree/opaque before init calls.

objects.definition:
typedef struct zng_gz_header_s {
    int32_t         text;       /* true if compressed data believed to be text */
    unsigned long   time;       /* modification time */
    int32_t         xflags;     /* extra flags (not used when writing a gzip file) */
    int32_t         os;         /* operating system */
    uint8_t         *extra;     /* pointer to extra field or NULL if none */
    uint32_t        extra_len;  /* extra field length (valid if extra != NULL) */
    uint32_t        extra_max;  /* space at extra (only when reading header) */
    uint8_t         *name;      /* pointer to zero-terminated file name or NULL */
    uint32_t        name_max;   /* space at name (only when reading header) */
    uint8_t         *comment;   /* pointer to zero-terminated comment or NULL */
    uint32_t        comm_max;   /* space at comment (only when reading header) */
    int32_t         hcrc;       /* true if there was or will be a header crc */
    int32_t         done;       /* true when done reading gzip header (not used when writing a gzip file) */
} zng_gz_header;

typedef zng_gz_header *zng_gz_headerp;
objects.description: Gzip header metadata container for supplying or retrieving gzip header fields when compressing/decompressing with gzip wrapping.
Abbreviated, exposed portion of the internal gzip file state used to support the zng_gzgetc macro. Not for direct manipulation by applications.
Callback function type supplying input to zng_inflateBack. Returns number of input bytes and sets pointer to buffer.
Callback function type consuming output from zng_inflateBack. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure.
Enumeration of deflate stream tunable parameter identifiers used with zng_deflateSetParams/GetParams.
Parameter value carrier used to set/get multiple deflate parameters in batch. Each entry specifies id, buffer, size, and per-parameter status.

functions.name: zlibng_version
functions.description: Returns a string with the zlib-ng library version. Useful for run-time vs. compile-time version checks and diagnostics.
requirements: None; may be called at any time.

functions.name: zng_deflateInit
functions.description: Initialize a zng_stream for compression using default settings. Sets internal state; no compression is performed.
requirements: strm must be a valid pointer.
Before calling, set strm->zalloc, strm->zfree, and strm->opaque (set to Z_NULL to use defaults).
level must be Z_DEFAULT_COMPRESSION or an integer in [0,9].
On success, total_in, total_out, adler, and msg are initialized.
Returns Z_OK on success; Z_MEM_ERROR on allocation failure; Z_STREAM_ERROR on invalid level.

functions.name: zng_deflate
functions.description: Compresses input to output according to flush policy. May need to be called repeatedly as it consumes input and/or fills output.
requirements: strm must be an initialized compression stream via deflateInit/deflateInit2/deflateReset.
Before each call, provide input and/or output space: ensure strm->avail_in > 0 or strm->avail_out > 0, and next_in/next_out non-NULL accordingly.
strm->avail_out must not be zero on entry unless only pending output needs flushing with Z_FINISH/Z_*_FLUSH.
flush must be one of Z_NO_FLUSH, Z_PARTIAL_FLUSH, Z_SYNC_FLUSH, Z_FULL_FLUSH, Z_FINISH, or Z_BLOCK.
If deflate returns Z_OK with strm->avail_out == 0, provide more output space and call again with the same flush until non-zero avail_out.
For single-call compression using Z_FINISH, ensure output buffer size >= deflateBound(sourceLen).
When generating gzip (via deflateInit2), strm->adler is CRC-32; otherwise Adler-32.
Return codes: Z_OK (progress), Z_STREAM_END (finished, only with Z_FINISH), Z_STREAM_ERROR (bad state/NULL pointers), Z_BUF_ERROR (no progress; e.g., zero avail_in/out).

functions.name: zng_deflateEnd
functions.description: Ends a compression stream and frees all internal allocations. Discards unprocessed input and does not flush pending output.
requirements: strm must have been initialized for deflate.
After return, stream is no longer usable unless reinitialized (e.g., deflateInit).
Returns Z_OK on success; Z_STREAM_ERROR on inconsistent state; Z_DATA_ERROR if stream was freed prematurely (unprocessed input/output).

functions.name: zng_inflateInit
functions.description: Initialize a zng_stream for decompression with default zlib-wrapped input. Allocation of the window may be deferred until first inflate() call.
requirements: strm must be a valid pointer.
Before calling, set next_in, avail_in, zalloc, zfree, and opaque (zalloc/zfree may be Z_NULL to use defaults).
On success, total_in, total_out, adler, and msg are initialized.
Returns Z_OK on success; Z_MEM_ERROR on allocation failure; Z_STREAM_ERROR on invalid parameters (e.g., null strm).

functions.name: zng_inflate
functions.description: Decompresses input to output according to flush policy. May need to be called repeatedly until Z_STREAM_END or an error.
requirements: strm must be an initialized inflate stream via inflateInit/inflateInit2/inflateReset.
Before each call, ensure either there is available input (avail_in>0) and/or output space (avail_out>0); set next_in/next_out accordingly.
flush must be one of Z_NO_FLUSH, Z_SYNC_FLUSH, Z_FINISH, Z_BLOCK, or Z_TREES.
If Z_FINISH is used for a single-step inflate, ensure avail_out is large enough to hold the entire uncompressed data.
When Z_BLOCK or Z_TREES is used, be prepared for early returns at block boundaries; consult strm->data_type bits as documented.
If Z_NEED_DICT is returned, call inflateSetDictionary with the matching dictionary before continuing.

Return codes: Z_OK (progress), Z_STREAM_END (all output produced), Z_NEED_DICT, Z_DATA_ERROR (corrupt/format error), Z_STREAM_ERROR (bad state/NULL pointers), Z_MEM_ERROR (allocation failure), Z_BUF_ERROR (no progress or insufficient space with Z_FINISH).

functions.name: zng_inflateEnd
functions.description: Ends a decompression stream and frees all internal allocations. Discards unprocessed input and does not flush pending output.
requirements: strm must have been initialized for inflate.
After return, stream is no longer usable unless reinitialized (e.g., inflateInit).
Returns Z_OK on success; Z_STREAM_ERROR on inconsistent state.

functions.name: zng_deflateInit2
functions.signature: int32_t zng_deflateInit2(zng_stream *strm, int32_t level, int32_t method, int32_t windowBits, int32_t memLevel, int32_t strategy);
functions.description: Initialize a compression stream with explicit parameters including method, window size, memory level, and strategy. No compression performed.
requirements: strm must be valid; set zalloc, zfree, opaque before calling (Z_NULL allowed for defaults).
method must be Z_DEFLATED.

windowBits: 8..15 for zlib wrapper; -8..-15 for raw deflate; add 16 to request gzip wrapper. Value 8 maps to 9 internally for deflate; do not pair with inflateInit2(8). For raw/gzip, a 256-byte window (|windowBits|==8) is invalid and rejected.
memLevel: 1..9 (1=min memory/slow, 9=max memory/fast). Default 8.
strategy: Z_DEFAULT_STRATEGY, Z_FILTERED, Z_HUFFMAN_ONLY, Z_RLE, or Z_FIXED.
Returns Z_OK on success; Z_MEM_ERROR on memory failure; Z_STREAM_ERROR on invalid parameters.

functions.name: zng_deflateSetDictionary
functions.signature: int32_t zng_deflateSetDictionary(zng_stream *strm, const uint8_t *dictionary, uint32_t dictLength);
functions.description: Preload a compression dictionary. For zlib wrapper, must be called immediately after initialization/reset and before any deflate(). For raw deflate, call before any deflate or exactly at a block boundary.
requirements: strm must be an initialized deflate stream.
dictionary must be non-NULL when dictLength>0.
For zlib wrapper: call immediately after deflateInit/deflateInit2/deflateReset and before first deflate().
For raw deflate: call before first deflate() or right after completing a block (all input consumed and output delivered) when using Z_BLOCK/Z_PARTIAL_FLUSH/Z_SYNC_FLUSH/Z_FULL_FLUSH.
Effective usable dictionary may be truncated by window size; at most window - 262 bytes are used.
On return, strm->adler is set to the Adler-32 of dictionary (not for raw).
Returns Z_OK on success; Z_STREAM_ERROR on invalid parameter or inconsistent state.

functions.name: zng_deflateGetDictionary
functions.description: Retrieve the current sliding dictionary from an active deflate stream.
requirements: strm must be a valid, initialized deflate stream.
If dictionary is non-NULL, it must have space for up to 32768 bytes; exactly *dictLength bytes are written.
If dictionary is NULL, only *dictLength is set.
If dictLength is NULL, the length is not returned.
Returned length may be less than window size (by up to 258 bytes).
Returns Z_OK on success; Z_STREAM_ERROR if stream state is inconsistent.

functions.name: zng_deflateCopy
functions.description: Deep-copies the entire compression state from source to dest. Useful for strategy exploration but can be slow and memory-heavy.
requirements: source must be a valid, initialized deflate stream; dest must be a valid pointer.
dest must not point to the same object as source.
Returns Z_OK on success; Z_MEM_ERROR on allocation failure; Z_STREAM_ERROR on inconsistent source (e.g., zalloc NULL).

functions.name: zng_deflateReset
functions.description: Reset a deflate stream as if deflateEnd followed by deflateInit, without freeing and reallocating the internal state. Keeps compression level and attributes.
requirements: strm must be a valid, initialized deflate stream.
On success, total_in, total_out, adler, and msg are reinitialized.
Returns Z_OK on success; Z_STREAM_ERROR on inconsistent state (e.g., NULL zalloc/state).

functions.name: zng_deflateParams
functions.signature: int32_t zng_deflateParams(zng_stream *strm, int32_t level, int32_t strategy);
functions.description: Dynamically change compression level and/or strategy mid-stream. May trigger an internal Z_BLOCK flush of pending input using the old parameters.
requirements: strm must be a valid deflate stream.
level and strategy as per deflateInit2.
If an internal deflate(Z_BLOCK) lacks output space, parameters are not changed and Z_BUF_ERROR is returned; retry with more output space.
To ensure change takes effect on first try, flush with deflate(Z_BLOCK or others) until avail_out != 0, and do not provide more input before calling deflateParams().
Returns Z_OK on success; Z_STREAM_ERROR on invalid parameters/state; Z_BUF_ERROR if not enough output space to complete compression of queued input before parameter change.

functions.name: zng_deflateTune
functions.signature: int32_t zng_deflateTune(zng_stream *strm, int32_t good_length, int32_t max_lazy, int32_t nice_length, int32_t max_chain);
functions.description: Fine-tune internal deflate match parameters for expert use to squeeze maximal compression for specific data.
requirements: strm must be a valid deflate stream (after deflateInit/deflateInit2).
Parameters must be chosen with understanding of deflate internals (see source); no documented numeric constraints beyond type ranges.
Returns Z_OK on success; Z_STREAM_ERROR on invalid deflate stream.

functions.name: zng_deflateBound
functions.signature: unsigned long zng_deflateBound(zng_stream *strm, unsigned long sourceLen);
functions.description: Returns an upper bound on compressed size for deflating sourceLen bytes with the current stream settings. Useful for sizing single-pass output buffers.
requirements: strm must be initialized for deflate, and after deflateSetHeader() if used.
sourceLen is the input size to be compressed in one pass.
If first deflate() is called with exactly sourceLen input, an output buffer of this size and flush=Z_FINISH guarantees Z_STREAM_END.
Bounds may be exceeded if using flush modes other than Z_FINISH or Z_NO_FLUSH.

functions.name: zng_deflatePending
functions.description: Report how many full bytes and residual bits of compressed data are pending but not yet emitted due to limited avail_out.
requirements: strm must be a valid deflate stream.
If pending or bits is NULL, that value is not set.
bits will be 0..7.
Returns Z_OK on success; Z_STREAM_ERROR on inconsistent state.

functions.name: zng_deflatePrime
functions.signature: int32_t zng_deflatePrime(zng_stream *strm, int32_t bits, int32_t value);
functions.description: Insert up to 16 bits into the beginning of the deflate output stream to prepend leftover bits when appending raw deflate streams. Only for raw deflate and before the first deflate() call after init/reset.
requirements: strm must be a valid deflate stream initialized via deflateInit2() or deflateReset() for raw deflate.
Call before the first deflate() after initialization/reset.
bits must be in [0,16]; the least significant bits of value are used.
Returns Z_OK on success; Z_BUF_ERROR if insufficient internal buffer space; Z_STREAM_ERROR on inconsistent state.

functions.name: zng_deflateSetHeader
functions.description: Provide gzip header fields to be written for streams initialized with gzip encoding (deflateInit2 with windowBits+16).
requirements: strm must be a valid deflate stream configured for gzip via deflateInit2().
Call after deflateInit2()/deflateReset() and before first deflate().
If head->name/comment are non-NULL, they must be NUL-terminated; if head->extra is non-NULL, head->extra_len bytes must be available.
If head->hcrc is true, a header CRC will be included.
Returns Z_OK on success; Z_STREAM_ERROR on inconsistent stream state.

functions.name: zng_inflateInit2
functions.description: Initialize a decompression stream with explicit window and wrapper settings (zlib, raw, gzip, or auto-detect).
requirements: strm must be valid; set next_in, avail_in, zalloc, zfree, opaque before calling (zalloc/zfree may be Z_NULL).
windowBits: 8..15 for zlib; 0 to use window size from zlib header; -8..-15 for raw; 15+16 for gzip only; 15+32 for zlib/gzip auto-detect.
windowBits must be >= the compressor’s deflateInit2() windowBits (magnitude) or equal to 15 if compressor’s is unknown; otherwise inflate() returns Z_DATA_ERROR.
Returns Z_OK; Z_MEM_ERROR on memory failure; Z_STREAM_ERROR on invalid parameters. May consume zlib header bytes; next_out/avail_out are unused at init.

functions.name: zng_inflateSetDictionary
functions.signature: int32_t zng_inflateSetDictionary(zng_stream *strm, const uint8_t *dictionary, uint32_t dictLength);
functions.description: Provide the decompression dictionary required after inflate() returns Z_NEED_DICT. For raw inflate, may be called at any time to amend the window.
requirements: strm must be a valid inflate stream.
Call immediately after an inflate() that returned Z_NEED_DICT (for wrapped formats).
dictionary must match the Adler-32 reported by inflate (for wrapped formats).
For raw inflate, may be called anytime; if provided dictionary < window and window already contains data, dictionary is appended/amended.
Returns Z_OK on success; Z_STREAM_ERROR on invalid parameters/state; Z_DATA_ERROR if dictionary does not match expected Adler-32.

functions.name: zng_inflateGetDictionary
functions.description: Retrieve the current sliding dictionary from an active inflate stream.
requirements: strm must be a valid inflate stream.
If dictionary is non-NULL, it must have space for up to 32768 bytes; exactly *dictLength bytes are written.
If dictionary is NULL, only *dictLength is set.
If dictLength is NULL, the length is not returned.
Returns Z_OK on success; Z_STREAM_ERROR if stream state is inconsistent.

functions.name: zng_inflateSync
functions.description: Skip invalid compressed data to find a possible full-flush point (00 00 FF FF). Provides no output; assists partial recovery.
requirements: strm must be a valid inflate stream with input provided in next_in/avail_in.
Returns Z_OK if a possible full flush point found; Z_BUF_ERROR if no more input provided; Z_DATA_ERROR if none found; Z_STREAM_ERROR on inconsistent stream.

functions.name: zng_inflateCopy
functions.description: Deep-copies the entire inflate state from source to dest for random access or checkpointing.
requirements: source must be a valid, initialized inflate stream; dest must be a valid pointer.
dest must not alias source.
Returns Z_OK on success; Z_MEM_ERROR on allocation failure; Z_STREAM_ERROR on inconsistent source (e.g., zalloc NULL).

functions.name: zng_inflateReset
functions.description: Reset a decompression stream as if inflateEnd followed by inflateInit, without freeing/reallocating internal state. Keeps attributes from inflateInit2.
requirements: strm must be a valid inflate stream.
On success, total_in, total_out, adler, and msg are reinitialized.
Returns Z_OK on success; Z_STREAM_ERROR on inconsistent state.

functions.name: zng_inflateReset2
functions.description: Reset an inflate stream and optionally change wrap/window settings like inflateInit2. May free existing window; will be reallocated on demand.
requirements: strm must be a valid inflate stream.
windowBits interpreted as in inflateInit2 (range/meaning identical).
Returns Z_OK on success; Z_STREAM_ERROR on inconsistent state or invalid windowBits.

functions.name: zng_inflatePrime
functions.signature: int32_t zng_inflatePrime(zng_stream *strm, int32_t bits, int32_t value);
functions.description: Preload up to 16 bits into the inflate input bit buffer (or clear it with negative bits) to align starting position, typically for raw inflate.
requirements: strm must be a valid inflate stream used for raw deflate.
Call before the first inflate() after inflateInit2()/inflateReset().
If bits >= 0, bits must be in [0,16]; least significant bits of value are inserted.
If bits < 0, the input bit buffer is cleared.
Returns Z_OK on success; Z_STREAM_ERROR on inconsistent state.

functions.name: zng_inflateMark
functions.description: Report internal decode position: lower 16 bits is bytes already emitted for current code; upper bits encode state as documented (e.g., -1 with lower 0 means between blocks; -1 with lower non-zero means inside stored block).
requirements: strm must be a valid inflate stream.
Caller must parse the return value per documentation.
Returns -65536 on inconsistent stream.

functions.name: zng_inflateGetHeader
functions.description: Request storage of parsed gzip header fields during inflate. head->done indicates completion; -1 indicates non-gzip input. Can force early return using Z_BLOCK or Z_TREES.
requirements: strm must be a valid inflate stream initialized via inflateInit2()/inflateReset().
Call before first inflate().
If head->extra non-NULL, set extra_max to buffer size. name/comment buffers must be provided and sized (name_max/comm_max) and will be NUL-terminated unless truncated.
On absence of fields, respective pointers are set to NULL if provided.
Returned fields may point into supplied buffers; application must manage lifetimes of any allocated memory it provided.
Returns Z_OK on success; Z_STREAM_ERROR on inconsistent stream.

functions.name: zng_inflateBackInit
functions.description: Initialize a stream for callback-based raw inflate via inflateBack(). The caller supplies the window buffer.
requirements: strm must be valid; set zalloc, zfree, opaque before calling (Z_NULL allowed for defaults).
windowBits must be in [8,15]; for general deflate streams, use 15 and provide a 32K window.
window must point to at least 1<<windowBits bytes.
Returns Z_OK on success; Z_STREAM_ERROR on invalid parameters; Z_MEM_ERROR if internal state allocation fails.

functions.name: zng_inflateBack
functions.signature: int32_t zng_inflateBack(zng_stream *strm, in_func in, void *in_desc, out_func out, void *out_desc);
functions.description: Perform a complete raw inflate using input/output callbacks and a caller-provided window (from inflateBackInit). Avoids copying by using the window as the output buffer.
requirements: strm must have been initialized with inflateBackInit() and have next_in/avail_in optionally set for initial input.
in must be a callback: uint32_t in(void *in_desc, const uint8_t **buf); return 0 on no input (buf ignored).

out must be a callback: int32_t out(void *out_desc, uint8_t *buf, uint32_t len); return 0 on success, non-zero on failure. It must not modify the provided window buffer contents and will be called with len <= window size.
in/out must not change the contents of the window provided to inflateBackInit().
On return, strm->next_in/avail_in indicate unused input from last in() call.
Returns Z_STREAM_END on success; Z_BUF_ERROR if in() returned 0 or out() returned non-zero; Z_DATA_ERROR on format error (strm->msg set); Z_STREAM_ERROR if not properly initialized.
in() is always called before out(); Z_BUF_ERROR due to out() can be distinguished because strm->next_in will be non-NULL.

functions.name: zng_inflateBackEnd
functions.description: Free all memory allocated by inflateBackInit().
requirements: strm must have been initialized by inflateBackInit().
Returns Z_OK on success; Z_STREAM_ERROR on inconsistent state.

functions.name: zng_zlibCompileFlags
functions.description: Return a bitfield of compile-time options, sizes, and feature selections of the library (see header documentation for bit meanings).
requirements: None.

functions.name: zng_compress
functions.signature: int32_t zng_compress(uint8_t *dest, size_t *destLen, const uint8_t *source, size_t sourceLen);
functions.description: Convenience one-shot compression with default level. Writes compressed data into dest.
requirements: dest must point to a buffer of at least compressBound(sourceLen) bytes.
*destLen must be set to the total size of dest on entry; set to actual compressed size on return.
source/sourceLen define input buffer.
Returns Z_OK; Z_MEM_ERROR on memory failure; Z_BUF_ERROR if dest size insufficient.

functions.name: zng_compress2
functions.signature: int32_t zng_compress2(uint8_t *dest, size_t *destLen, const uint8_t *source, size_t sourceLen, int32_t level);
functions.description: One-shot compression with explicit level.
requirements: dest must point to a buffer of at least compressBound(sourceLen) bytes.
*destLen set to total size on entry; set to actual compressed size on return.
level must be Z_DEFAULT_COMPRESSION or [0,9].
Returns Z_OK; Z_MEM_ERROR if out of memory; Z_BUF_ERROR if dest too small; Z_STREAM_ERROR if level invalid.

functions.name: zng_compressBound
functions.description: Compute an upper bound on the output size of compress()/compress2() for sourceLen bytes.
requirements: sourceLen is the input size to be compressed.

functions.name: zng_uncompress
functions.signature: int32_t zng_uncompress(uint8_t *dest, size_t *destLen, const uint8_t *source, size_t sourceLen);
functions.description: One-shot decompression of source into dest. dest must be large enough to hold the entire uncompressed data.
requirements: dest must point to a buffer large enough for the entire uncompressed size (must be known via external mechanism).
*destLen set to total dest size on entry; set to actual uncompressed size on return.
Returns Z_OK; Z_MEM_ERROR on memory failure; Z_BUF_ERROR if dest too small (partial output may be produced); Z_DATA_ERROR on corrupt/incomplete input.

functions.name: zng_uncompress2
functions.signature: int32_t zng_uncompress2(uint8_t *dest, size_t *destLen, const uint8_t *source, size_t *sourceLen);
functions.description: Like uncompress(), but sourceLen is an in/out parameter updated to report the number of source bytes consumed.
requirements: dest must be large enough for the entire uncompressed data.
On entry, *destLen is dest capacity; on return, set to actual uncompressed size.
On entry, *sourceLen is source size; on return, set to bytes consumed.
Returns Z_OK; Z_MEM_ERROR; Z_BUF_ERROR if dest too small; Z_DATA_ERROR on corrupt/incomplete input.

functions.name: zng_adler32
functions.signature: uint32_t zng_adler32(uint32_t adler, const uint8_t *buf, uint32_t len);
functions.description: Update an Adler-32 checksum with len bytes from buf, returning the updated value. If buf is Z_NULL, returns the initial value.
requirements: adler is the starting checksum (use 0 with buf==NULL and len==0 for initial).
buf may be Z_NULL to obtain initial value.
len is the number of bytes to process.

functions.name: zng_adler32_z
functions.signature: uint32_t zng_adler32_z(uint32_t adler, const uint8_t *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Same as zng_adler32, but len is size_t.
requirements: Same as zng_adler32, using size_t for len.

functions.name: zng_adler32_combine
functions.signature: uint32_t zng_adler32_combine(uint32_t adler1, uint32_t adler2, z_off64_t len2);
functions.description: Combine two Adler-32 checksums to obtain the checksum of the concatenation. len2 is the length of the second sequence.
requirements: len2 should be non-negative; if negative the result is meaningless.
adler1/adler2 are checksums of first/second sequences respectively.

functions.name: zng_crc32
functions.signature: uint32_t zng_crc32(uint32_t crc, const uint8_t *buf, uint32_t len);
functions.description: Update a CRC-32 with len bytes from buf, returning the updated value. If buf is Z_NULL, returns the initial value. Pre/post conditioning is handled internally.
requirements: crc is the starting CRC (use 0 with buf==NULL and len==0 for initial).
buf may be Z_NULL to obtain initial value.
len is bytes to process.

functions.name: zng_crc32_z

requirements: strm must be a valid deflate stream.
params points to an array of count entries; each entry’s buf/size must contain the value for the specified parameter ID.
If any buffer too small for the parameter value or duplicate parameter IDs are provided, returns Z_BUF_ERROR and no other changes are performed; inspect per-entry status to find offenders.

Returns Z_OK on success; Z_STREAM_ERROR if stream state is inconsistent or any value cannot be updated (per-entry status indicates which); Z_VERSION_ERROR if at least one parameter is unsupported (per-entry status indicates which).
Per-entry status values indicate success (Z_OK) or failure; if all are not Z_STREAM_ERROR but function returned Z_STREAM_ERROR, the error was due to stream state inconsistency.

import random
import struct
import zlib
from typing import List, Tuple

# Goal: generate valid, interesting arbitrary binary buffers suitable for zlib-ng fuzz stubs.
# Strategy:
# - Produce a mixture of valid zlib, gzip, and raw deflate streams of small sizes.
# - Include buffers that represent likely dictionaries or repetitive patterns.
# - Include edge-case sizes (0, small, moderate up to 1024 bytes) and content diversity.
# - Keep output <= 4096 bytes.
# - Deterministic per seed but random across seeds.

# Helpers to build gzip members

def _gzip_member(payload: bytes, mtime: int, fname: bytes | None, comment: bytes | None, xtra: bytes | None, xflags: int, osid: int, hcrc: bool) -> bytes:
    # Minimal gzip header: ID1 ID2 CM FLG MTIME XFL OS [extra] [name] [comment] [HCRC]
    ID1, ID2, CM = 0x1F, 0x8B, 8
    FLG = 0
    extra = b""
    name = b""
    comm = b""
    if xtra:
        FLG |= 0x04
        extra = struct.pack('<H', len(xtra)) + xtra
    if fname is not None:
        FLG |= 0x08
        name = fname + b"\x00"
    if comment is not None:
        FLG |= 0x10
        comm = comment + b"\x00"
    if hcrc:
        FLG |= 0x02
    header = bytes([ID1, ID2, CM, FLG]) + struct.pack('<I', mtime & 0xFFFFFFFF) + bytes([xflags & 0xFF, osid & 0xFF]) + extra + name + comm
    if hcrc:
        # CRC16 of header so far (as per gzip). Use zlib.crc32 then fold to 16 bits.
        crc = zlib.crc32(header) & 0xFFFF
        header += struct.pack('<H', crc)
    # Deflate-compress payload as DEFLATE blocks with default zlib module using raw DEFLATE? zlib requires wbits= -15 for raw.
    # However gzip expects deflate stream without zlib header. Use zlib.compressobj with wbits = -zlib.MAX_WBITS.
    comp = zlib.compressobj(level=6, wbits=-zlib.MAX_WBITS)
    body = comp.compress(payload) + comp.flush()
    # Trailer: CRC32 (of uncompressed) and ISIZE (mod 2^32)
    trailer = struct.pack('<II', zlib.crc32(payload) & 0xFFFFFFFF, len(payload) & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    return header + body + trailer


def _make_zlib_stream(payload: bytes, level: int = 6) -> bytes:
    # Standard zlib-wrapped deflate (wbits=+MAX_WBITS)
    return zlib.compress(payload, level)


def _make_raw_deflate(payload: bytes, level: int = 6) -> bytes:
    co = zlib.compressobj(level=level, wbits=-zlib.MAX_WBITS)
    return co.compress(payload) + co.flush()


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _pattern_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Build a buffer with mixed patterns to exercise compression ratios
    chunks: List[bytes] = []
    while sum(len(c) for c in chunks) < n:
        choice = rng.randrange(6)
        remain = n - sum(len(c) for c in chunks)
        if choice == 0:
            # Repeated single byte
            b = rng.randrange(256)
            rep = min(remain, 1 + rng.randrange(1, 128))
            chunks.append(bytes([b]) * rep)
        elif choice == 1:
            # Incrementing sequence
            length = min(remain, 1 + rng.randrange(1, 256))
            start = rng.randrange(256)
            seq = bytes((start + i) % 256 for i in range(length))
            chunks.append(seq)
        elif choice == 2:
            # Small dictionary-like word repeated
            word_len = 2 + rng.randrange(1, 16)
            word = _rand_bytes(rng, word_len)
            reps = min(1 + rng.randrange(1, 64), max(1, remain // max(1, word_len)))
            chunks.append(word * reps)  # may exceed remain; we will cut later
        elif choice == 3:
            # Zero run
            run = min(remain, 1 + rng.randrange(1, 512))
            chunks.append(b"\x00" * run)
        elif choice == 4:
            # ASCII text slice
            text = (b"Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. "
                    b"Sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua. ")
            reps = min(remain // len(text) + 1, 8)
            blob = (text * reps)[:remain]
            chunks.append(blob)
        else:
            # Random bytes block
            length = min(remain, 1 + rng.randrange(1, 256))
            chunks.append(_rand_bytes(rng, length))
    data = b"".join(chunks)
    return data[:n]


def _choose_lengths(rng: random.Random) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    # Choose source length and target max size for generated buffer
    # Focus on small inputs (0..1024), sometimes larger but keep <= 4096
    sizes = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 15, 31, 64, 128, 256, 512, 768, 1024]
    src_len = rng.choice(sizes)
    # Occasionally pick random within 0..1024
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        src_len = rng.randrange(0, 1025)
    max_out = 4096
    return src_len, max_out


def _make_dictionary(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Build plausible dictionary contents
    length = rng.randrange(0, min(max_len, 1024) + 1)
    if length == 0:
        return b""
    return _pattern_bytes(rng, length)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide which kind of buffer to produce
    # Weighted towards valid compressed streams that inflate can consume, but also include raw and random.
    kind = rng.choices(
        ["zlib", "gzip", "raw_deflate", "plain", "compound_gzip", "edge_random"],
        weights=[30, 25, 15, 15, 10, 5], k=1
    )[0]

    src_len, max_out = _choose_lengths(rng)
    payload = _pattern_bytes(rng, src_len)

    if kind == "zlib":
        level = rng.randrange(-1, 10)
        try:
            out = _make_zlib_stream(payload, level)
        except Exception:
            # Fallback to plain payload if compression fails unexpectedly
            out = payload
    elif kind == "gzip":
        # Construct gzip with varying header fields
        mtime = rng.randrange(0, 1 << 32)
        fname = None if rng.random() < 0.5 else _pattern_bytes(rng, rng.randrange(1, 16))
        comment = None if rng.random() < 0.6 else _pattern_bytes(rng, rng.randrange(1, 32))
        xtra = None if rng.random() < 0.7 else _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randrange(0, 32))
        xflags = rng.randrange(0, 256)
        osid = rng.randrange(0, 256)
        hcrc = rng.random() < 0.3
        out = _gzip_member(payload, mtime, fname, comment, xtra, xflags, osid, hcrc)
    elif kind == "raw_deflate":
        level = rng.randrange(0, 10)
        out = _make_raw_deflate(payload, level)
    elif kind == "compound_gzip":
        # Concatenate multiple gzip members (valid concatenation). Useful for inflate loops.
        members = []
        count = 2 + rng.randrange(0, 3)  # 2..4 members
        for _ in range(count):
            pl = _pattern_bytes(rng, rng.randrange(0, 512))
            m = _gzip_member(pl, rng.randrange(0, 1 << 32), None, None, None, 0, 255, False)
            members.append(m)
        out = b"".join(members)
    elif kind == "edge_random":
        # Edge-case raw bytes, including known zlib/gzip headers with truncated bodies within 4096
        choices: List[bytes] = []
        # Empty
        choices.append(b"")
        # Minimal zlib header for default window (CMF=0x78, FLG varies). Use 0x9C/0xDA/0x01 variants as common.
        choices.append(b"\x78\x9C")
        choices.append(b"\x78\xDA")
        choices.append(b"\x78\x01")
        # Gzip header only (no body)
        choices.append(b"\x1F\x8B\x08\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\xFF")
        # Some repeated bytes
        choices.append(b"A" * 64)
        choices.append(b"\x00" * 256)
        # Random chunk
        choices.append(_rand_bytes(rng, rng.randrange(1, 512)))
        out = rng.choice(choices)
    else:  # plain
        # Plain dictionary-like or random buffer for checksum and SetDictionary APIs
        dict_bias = rng.random() < 0.5
        out = _make_dictionary(rng, 1024) if dict_bias else payload

    # Ensure size bound
    if len(out) > max_out:
        out = out[:max_out]

    return out

import random
import struct
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets fuzzers that consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR() for gzip header fields
# used with zng_deflateSetHeader and zng_inflateGetHeader. Those expect C strings
# (NUL-terminated) for name/comment, and a byte string for extra. The harness will
# NUL-terminate again, but it also treats empty std::string as a null pointer. We
# therefore sometimes return empty buffers (to produce nullptr) and sometimes return
# meaningful NUL-terminated names/comments and plausible gzip extra fields. The
# harness also requests several unsigned ints via FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int); we pack
# those as 4-byte little-endian blobs so that the provider can parse them as needed.

# We produce a composite buffer that the fuzzer will slice sequentially:
# 1) name string (C string, <= 64 chars including terminating NUL in harness)
# 2) comment string (same constraints)
# 3) extra field bytes (<= 128 bytes; may include subfields like FEXTRA items)
# 4) a sequence of unsigned ints for text, time, xflags, os, hcrc
# The stub calls FUZZ_PARAM_STR three times and a few FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int).
# Our provider typically feeds these sequentially from the same input corpus.


def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Favor typical filename/comment characters; include some edge cases
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-.,+/@()[]{}~#%$^&!" \
        + "\t"  # include a tab occasionally
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))
    return s.encode('utf-8', 'ignore')


ess_ids = [
    # Common gzip extra subfield IDs
    b"BC",  # Brotli dictionary or generic
    b"RA",  # Random/access hints
    b"SL",  # OS-specific
    b"XL",  # extra length test
    b"ZZ",  # unknown/custom
    b"FH",  # file hint
]


def _build_gzip_extra(rng: random.Random, max_total: int = 128) -> bytes:
    # Build a valid gzip FEXTRA-style payload: sequence of
    # (2-byte ID, 2-byte little-endian data length, data)
    # staying within max_total bytes.
    remaining = max_total
    out = bytearray()
    # Randomly decide to return empty extra sometimes
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        return b""
    # Add 1-4 subfields
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4)):
        if remaining < 4:
            break
        sid = rng.choice(ess_ids)
        if len(sid) != 2:
            sid = sid[:2].ljust(2, b"X")
        # choose a data length that fits
        max_len = min(remaining - 4, rng.randint(0, 48))
        data_len = rng.randint(0, max(0, max_len))
        data = rng.randbytes(data_len) if data_len > 0 else b""
        out += sid
        out += struct.pack('<H', data_len)
        out += data
        remaining = max_total - len(out)
        if remaining <= 0:
            break
    return bytes(out[:max_total])


def _maybe_empty_cstr(rng: random.Random, content_builder) -> bytes:
    # 50% chance to return empty (so harness treats as nullptr). Otherwise build content and NUL-terminate.
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return b""  # empty => nullptr in harness
    data = content_builder()
    # Ensure there is no embedded NUL before the terminator to exercise typical C string behavior
    data = data.replace(b"\x00", b"")
    return data + b"\x00"


def _pack_uints(values: List[int]) -> bytes:
    # Pack as little-endian unsigned int (4 bytes each). Range-limited to 32-bit.
    b = bytearray()
    for v in values:
        b += struct.pack('<I', v & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    return bytes(b)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build name (C string terminated) with common filename-like patterns
    def name_builder() -> bytes:
        # Prefer shorter names sometimes, with and without extensions
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            base = _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 6)
        else:
            base = _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 20)
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            ext = rng.choice([b".txt", b".bin", b".log", b".dat", b".json", b".cfg", b".gz"])  # harmless extensions
            return base + ext
        return base

    name_cstr = _maybe_empty_cstr(rng, name_builder)

    # Build comment (C string)
    def comment_builder() -> bytes:
        # Include some human-ish text and versions
        parts = []
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            parts.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 3, 12))
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            parts.append(b"v" + str(rng.randint(0, 999)).encode())
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            parts.append(b"(test)")
        if not parts:
            parts = [_rand_ascii(rng, 1, 10)]
        return b" ".join(parts)

    comment_cstr = _maybe_empty_cstr(rng, comment_builder)

    # Build extra field bytes
    extra_bytes = _build_gzip_extra(rng, 128)

    # Unsigned ints for text (flag), time, xflags, os, hcrc.
    # text and hcrc are consumed as &1; xflags/os as &0xFF. time arbitrary.
    text_flag = rng.randint(0, 1)
    # Use plausible UNIX timestamps near present, but allow edge cases too
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        # Current-ish epoch +/- 5 years
        now = 1733961600  # ~2024-12-12 epoch for determinism anchor
        jitter = rng.randint(-5 * 365 * 86400, 5 * 365 * 86400)
        mtime = (now + jitter) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    else:
        mtime = rng.getrandbits(32)
    xflags = rng.choice([0, 2, 4, 8, 0x1E, 0xFF])
    os_code = rng.choice([
        0,   # FAT
        3,   # Unix
        7,   # Macintosh
        11,  # NTFS
        255  # unknown
    ])
    hcrc_flag = rng.randint(0, 1)

    uint_blob = _pack_uints([text_flag, mtime, xflags, os_code, hcrc_flag])

    # Concatenate in the order FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) will likely consume
    # The harness does: name STR, comment STR, extra STR, then several unsigned ints.
    # We place them in that order.
    out = bytearray()
    out += name_cstr
    out += comment_cstr
    out += extra_bytes
    out += uint_blob

    # Ensure reasonable total size and cap at 4096 bytes
    return bytes(out[:4096])
